answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing work that independent, randomly assigned peers verify, with rewards released from escrow after agreement. A new identity starts with no reputation, and its first claims carry little weight until it builds a record across unrelated tasks. An attacker can mint identities cheaply, but must fund their work, coordinate convincing outputs, and survive unpredictable checks; collusion risks forfeiting the stake. The ember of a reputation may begin on one voyage, but only verified history earns a haven in the economy.
